key_insight: This paper shows that sparse episode-level success/failure can be turned into richer transition-level training signal by weighting advantages hierarchically, instead of collapsing everything into one scalar reward. The result is more informative online fine-tuning for pretrained vision-language-action (VLA) policies.
problem_solved: Online RL fine-tuning of VLAs often gets only one binary outcome per rollout episode, but the actor still needs per-step supervision. Simple scalar rewards or advantages mix together different kinds of feedback and become less useful once the agent starts succeeding on easy cases.
method: Use hierarchical advantage weighting to map sparse episode outcomes into structured transition-level learning signals.
Separate distinct feedback sources instead of collapsing them into one global scalar advantage.
Apply the weighted signal during online RL fine-tuning to guide policy updates more effectively from success/failure-only data.
impact: This approach can make online RL fine-tuning more sample-efficient and more stable when feedback is extremely sparse. For practitioners, it offers a practical way to keep improving pretrained VLA agents beyond the point where basic task success is already achieved.

paper_title: Hierarchical Advantage Weighting for Online RL Fine-Tuning of VLAs from Sparse Episode Outcomes
paper_authors: Tongyan Fang, Siyuan Huang, Naiyu Fang, Ganlong Zhao, Zhongjin Luo
